title: Path Add Queries on a Tree
statement:
You are given a tree with `n` nodes numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Node `i` has an initial value `initial[i]`. You are also given `q` queries; query `j` is a triple `(u, v, x)`.

To process a query, add `x` to the value of **every node on the path from `u` to `v`**, including both endpoints (if `u = v`, the path is the single node `u`). `x` may be negative. All queries are applied, in any order, to the same tree.

After all queries have been applied, compute for every node the absolute difference between its updated value and its initial value, and print the **sum of these absolute differences over all nodes**.

Note that a node's total change is the sum of the `x` values of all queries whose path passes through it, so changes of different queries can cancel out before the absolute value is taken.

Tests keep the tree shallow enough for recursion: the depth of the tree when rooted at node `0` is at most 5000.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `initial[0] ... initial[n-1]`.
The next `n - 1` lines each contain two integers `a b`, an edge of the tree.
The next line contains `q`.
The next `q` lines each contain three integers `u v x`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the sum over all nodes of |updated value - initial value|.
constraints: The tree rooted at node 0 has depth at most 5000

examples.explanation: Query 1 adds 2 to nodes 3, 1, 4. Query 2 adds -1 to nodes 3, 1, 0, 2. Net changes: node 0: -1, node 1: 2 - 1 = 1, node 2: -1, node 3: 2 - 1 = 1, node 4: 2. The absolute values sum to 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6.
The first query adds 5 to all three nodes; the second adds -5 to node 1 only. Node 1 ends with a net change of 0, nodes 0 and 2 change by 5 each, so the answer is 10 (not 15 or 20).

hints: Updating each path node by node is O(n) per query. Think of a way to record an update at the two endpoints only, and spread it later.

On a rooted tree, a path update (u, v, x) is the same as +x at u, +x at v, -x at lca(u, v) and -x at the parent of lca(u, v). Then a single bottom-up pass sums each subtree to give every node's net change.
Find the LCA with binary lifting (or any other LCA method). The initial values never affect the answer.
